t1kqejni.name: Protests over India election chief
t1kqejni.latestHeadline: India’s voter roll overhaul fuels citizenship fears: ‘what if they ask us to leave?’
t1kqejni.summary: On 2 October, thousands of people joined a Mumbai protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party that asked the election chief to resign. In the days after, police detained dozens of protesters over changes to voter rolls, and on 6 October opposition MPs were detained, with opposition leaders alleging that CEC Gyanesh Kumar manipulated the rolls to favour PM Narendra Modi's party. By 10 October, police had ordered a virtual shutdown of New Delhi ahead of a planned protest and the country's highest court intervened, and on 12 October opposition parties and supporters of the youth movement marched towards the Supreme Court over the removal of millions of names from voter lists. By 16 October, protests had intensified in New Delhi, with critics calling the voter list review politically motivated while the Election Commission and Modi's administration denied the allegations.

events.headline: US arrests California man for allegedly smuggling $300m worth of computer servers to China
Mapping US chip supply chain: China accounts for far more than it appears, report says

t139atn9.summary: In early October, The Guardian reported that US authorities had arrested a California man, Greg Lui, for allegedly smuggling $300m worth of computer servers to China. He allegedly used false paperwork to move export-controlled gear from the US to third countries and then on to China. In mid-October, the South China Morning Post reported on a Semiconductor Industry Association report on the US chip supply chain. It found that China accounts for about 5 per cent of the equipment and materials directly supplied to the US chip industry by country of manufacture, but holds over 90 per cent of certain rare earths needed for chipmaking.

t1j5n1me.name: Yemen war and Houthi strikes
t1j5n1me.latestHeadline: Blast heard in Yemen’s Aden as Houthis claim attack on military camp
t1j5n1me.summary: On 4 October, Yemen's president announced an all-out war to reclaim land from the Houthis, amid an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition. Two days later, Saudi Arabia said three people were wounded when Houthi strikes hit the Jazan and Najran airports, and by 10 October Al Jazeera was reporting that fighting between government forces and the Houthis was intensifying. In mid-October, Saudi Arabia struck oil depots near Sana'a, Houthi missiles hit the Maashiq Palace in Aden, and the UAE reportedly agreed to re-enter the conflict, while Egypt, Pakistan and the UK moved to help defend Saudi Arabia. Between 19 and 21 October, a Houthi attack killed 53 people at a government training camp in Shabwa, Saudi Arabia postponed its Future Investment Initiative event after the attacks, and the Houthis claimed a missile attack on a military camp in Aden.

t1rn1bq5.summary: In early October, the euro fell to a 17-month low against the US dollar, with reports citing concerns about France's ability to bring its public finances in order and an announced snap election in Spain. France 24 reported that the currency had dropped nearly 7 percent from its peak in late January. In the week of October 22, French protests and mounting bond market pressure pushed France's 10-year government bond yield to a 24-year high. Around October 23, reports said French borrowing costs had surged as debt and political risks mounted, raising questions over whether the stress could spread across the euro zone, while Moody's left France's credit rating at Aa3.

t14axxk2.name: Black Sea shipping attacks
t14axxk2.latestHeadline: Romania blames Russia after drone sinks ship in the Black Sea
t14axxk2.summary: In early October, Ukraine's leader condemned a Russian strike on a Turkish-owned boat carrying corn in the Black Sea, in which the captain was killed and 11 crew were rescued. Around October 6, Bulgaria searched for missing crew after drones hit two ships and the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan sank, and on October 7 Russian authorities said an attack by "unmanned boats" on a Liberian-flagged tanker off Sochi sparked a huge oil fire. By mid-October, Bulgaria's prime minister said another drone attack off its coast had hit two ships, including the Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3, which was damaged. On October 20 Nato increased its Black Sea deployment, and on October 23 Romania blamed Russia after a drone sank the Comoros-flagged Khoryv, leaving one sailor dead and three missing.

t1ibmsov.latestHeadline: Ukraine launches over 1,000 drones at Russia, setting oil facilities ablaze
t1ibmsov.summary: In early October, Ukraine's top sanctions official said Russia had imported fuel from South Korean ports, easing a fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries. On October 11, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv was ready to halt refinery strikes if Moscow stopped attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure, and US President Donald Trump said both sides had agreed to an "energy ceasefire." By October 16, Zelensky said Ukraine would resume the strikes he had paused to comply with a US demand, Russian authorities said a major refinery southeast of Moscow had been hit, and Trump called the strikes a "disgrace" that keeps global energy prices elevated. On October 18 and 19, reports described Ukraine launching more than 1,000 drones at Russian oil and other facilities, while Zelensky said Moscow continued to break the energy ceasefire.

events.headline: India’s retail inflation jumps to 5.54% in September, above estimates

t1qk19hr.summary: In early October, India's central bank raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, with BBC News and CNBC reporting that the move reflected growing inflation concerns. BBC News described it as part of a global shift towards tighter monetary policy as central banks battle inflation fuelled by Middle East conflict. CNBC also reported that HSBC and Goldman Sachs expect the RBI to raise rates again in December. In mid-October, CNBC reported that India's retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September, above estimates, marking the 11th straight month of increase.

tq9ru94.summary: In early October, India, Turkiye, Egypt and the US put forward ceasefire proposals, and US envoys were set to meet Ukrainian and European officials in Miami to discuss a new proposal to end the war. By around October 10, the Kremlin said drone attacks on Moscow during last month's election had undermined trilateral talks, while President Trump called for Ukraine to replace President Zelensky. In mid-October, tensions between Washington and Kyiv deepened as Russia and Ukraine traded strikes, with Zelensky saying the two sides were still in near-constant contact. On October 21, Zelensky proposed freezing the front line as a first step toward peace talks as US envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin, and the Kremlin said it was ready to resume three-way talks in mid-November, though Russian missiles hit Kyiv the next day.

t1ya4ss.summary: In early October, BBC News profiled Neha Bora as one of the most recognisable faces of India's recent Gen Z-led protests. By mid-October, France 24 reported that the youth-led Cockroach movement was intensifying its protests against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, with three leaders detained after defying a ban at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site. On October 17, movement founder Abhijeet Dipke was picked up after two party leaders were arrested, and Jantar Mantar was denotified as a protest site. By October 21, UN experts called on India to stop using 'excessive force' against protesters and pressed for an independent investigation, while an Indian court ordered the release of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who had spent a week in jail.

t1vem20c.name: EU-China trade tensions
t1vem20c.latestHeadline: China slams EU’s potential new trade safeguards, says they may violate WTO rules
t1vem20c.summary: In early October, France's Emmanuel Macron and Germany's Friedrich Merz wrote to Ursula von der Leyen asking for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices, and reports noted that China's push to manufacture more at home had widened its trade imbalance with Europe. On 8 October, EU trade commissioner Maros Sefcovic arrived in Beijing for talks with Wang Wentao, saying he wanted to rebalance an "unsustainable trade deficit". By 12 October the EU announced a deal under which China would limit hybrid car exports to the bloc, with a quota of 350,000 a year. In mid-October EU leaders backed a trade "kill switch" tool as the bilateral deficit hit a record, and in late October the EU's trade chief said more Chinese industries could face quotas or tariffs, while Beijing said new safeguards might violate WTO rules.

tny4upw.summary: On October 8, the South China Morning Post reported that US President Donald Trump had pressed Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, during a summit the previous month, to end a deep freeze in relations with Japan's Sanae Takaichi. tpnacn3.latestHeadline: Inflation Accelerated in October, PCE Index Shows
tpnacn3.summary: In September 2026, the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years. On October 28 it held its benchmark rate steady, as expected, while chairman Kevin Warsh said the Fed would vote on rates seven times in 2027 and six in 2028, instead of the traditional eight. Ahead of that meeting, investors had thought a December rate hike was likely as the central bank tried to tamp down inflation. China seeks India’s help in defusing border tensions

t1rt9t5i.summary: On October 27, 2026, Al Jazeera reported that new India-China border face-offs were testing Modi six years after a deadly clash, and that they again challenged his strongman image at home despite a thaw in ties between the two countries. The next day, on October 28, the South China Morning Post reported that China said it would seek India's help to "maintain peace and stability in the border areas." It said this followed new stand-offs in a long-disputed region that threatened to undermine improved relations.

trijh54.name: US-India relations under Trump
trijh54.latestHeadline: Why India has soured on Trump ahead of US midterms
trijh54.summary: In late October 2026, The Guardian reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had not met Narendra Modi the previous week, which some saw as a snub, while his focus on business leaders and oil made American priorities clear. On October 28, the South China Morning Post reported that immigration restrictions, rising living costs and strains in US-India relations were testing support for President Trump among some Indian-Americans who backed the Republican Party in 2024, ahead of November's midterm elections. The same day, Al Jazeera wrote that, seven years after Modi backed Trump, New Delhi may now hope US midterm losses leave the president chastened.

events.headline: What Marco Rubio’s sidestepping of New Delhi says about the US’s stance on India

Can EU and India work together to secure Indo-Pacific?

t1t1f6ye.summary: On 28 October 2026, the South China Morning Post reported that India has become a major exporter of ammunition and other weapons to Europe since the outbreak of the Ukraine-Russia war. Analysts cautioned, however, that New Delhi has yet to secure a lasting foothold in Europe's defence market. The next day, 29 October, DW reported that India and Europe are deepening defence ties, but that their clashing perspectives on Russia and differing priorities on China are hampering their joint ambitions on maritime security.

t1ozb09t.name: ECB leadership and rate policy
t1ozb09t.latestHeadline: European Central Bank keeps key interest rate on hold at 2.5%
t1ozb09t.summary: On Thursday, 29 October 2026, European Central Bank president Christine Lagarde resigned, ending months of speculation about her future. The resignation came as Europe enters a period of rising economic volatility and divisive electoral politics, particularly in her native France. The same day, the ECB kept its key interest rate on hold at 2.5%, a decision markets saw as a hawkish pause, and they were last pricing in a 67% chance of a December rate hike.

events.headline: ECB head Lagarde resigns amid mounting economic, political challenges for Europe
